item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is probably the most simply creepy SCP I've read recently. Most of the creep comes not from the effect (I can think about literary gore all day without squeamishness), but from the plausible uses it was put to. First it was co-opted for communion (I was thinking this might be a genuine divine thing until I realized that this isn't sacremental equipment, but fine table settings). Then it was used to run a faux-long pork menu in the back room of a MC&D restaurant. That's not even that creepy- a lot of people have attempted to create faux-human meat (even supposedly a tofu-based variety IIRC). What's creepy is that a plausible subset of their elite clientelle wanted the "fake" human meat to be screaming in terror and pain as they ate!

Obviously, this is old, and doesn't need tests added, but I wonder:

  • What happens when human flesh is placed on/in SCP-604?
  • Will an infant animal transformed to an infant human develop normally?
  • If you used an anomalously small human (several SCP candidates) and placed them alive on/in SCP-604, what happens? Yes, cross testing is B-A-D(!!!!!), but I'm just brainstorming.

good stuff +1

…bizarre meals such as caramelized insects…

Dude, the point is "a set of tableware and dishes" that makes you eat human living flesh, I wouldn't go all "oh wow what a bizarre meal" about "caramelized insects" in such a context…
Anyway I like how this is based after the Christian communion, and the image of the swimming penis amuses me in a horrified way. Not to talk about how the guys in the logs seem just fine with it. Marshall, Carter and Dark Ltd sure is a sick bunch. Well done.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
That would first mean that the foundation used the same technique MC&D did to mutilate a live animal into the shape of a head.

But if they did that I could see the conversation going one of four ways:

  • The first is that the head is a blank slate, no name, no memories, it can talk but it really can't answer questions. Kinda boring but simple.
  • The second is that it is a copy of the part of another human and will have their memories. Inconsistent with the tone of the rest of the article being able to influence the hair line of the generated heads.
  • The third is that it is actually the transported part of someone, and somewhere out there there is a bunch of humans and babies missing their parts. Again, inconstant with the rest of the article and with the parts attempting locomotion under their own power.
  • Then there's my personal choice, that the head created knows everything. That the monks were in some way right. The created flesh is omnipotent because it is, not a blank slate, but one filled with all knowledge.
